brief: A 30 mm PLA cube with three 10 mm holes passing through its centre, one along each axis. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A 30 mm PLA cube with three mutually perpendicular 10 mm through-holes intersecting at its center, apparently a non-structural fixture or alignment/test piece.
stated: Holes pass through the centre, one along each axis (X, Y, Z)
User states it carries no load / no load case
implied: Since holes are along each of three axes and pass through centre, they must intersect each other at the cube's middle, implying a hollowed-out central cavity rather than three separate isolated bores
30 mm likely refers to edge length of the cube, implied by calling it a '30 mm cube'
PLA material implies FDM 3D-printed construction and associated anisotropic, layer-dependent properties
'No load' claim implies the part is decorative, demonstrative, or a test/calibration piece rather than a functional mechanical component
unstated: Exact cube dimensions if not uniform (confirm 30x30x30 mm, not just one edge)
Hole tolerance/fit class (e.g., for dowel pins, fasteners, or clearance only)
Whether the three holes are meant to be perfectly orthogonal and concentric through the geometric center, and alignment tolerance between them
Intended use/function of the holes (alignment, weight reduction, pass-through for cables/rods, aesthetic)
Print orientation or layer line direction, which matters for PLA strength even under 'no load' claim if the part is handled or dropped
Any chamfer/deburr requirements at hole intersections where three bores meet, since this intersection creates sharp internal edges and partial hole walls
Whether the hole axes pass exactly through the geometric center or are offset
Environmental conditions (indoor use, temperature, since PLA deforms around 50-60°C) despite 'no load' claim
Whether 'no load' includes handling, assembly, or incidental drops, or only in-service static loading
out_of_scope: No dimensions, materials, or geometry details beyond what is stated are being proposed here
risk_signals: None stated in the brief itself -- user explicitly claims no load case, and nothing suggests the part carries a person, lifts weight, holds pressure, stores energy, or is part of a vehicle/regulated equipment
PLA's low heat deflection temperature could be a latent risk if the part is later used in an unstated thermal environment, but this is not indicated by the brief

requirements.statement: The cube's overall width shall be 30 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief states a 30 mm cube.

requirements.statement: The cube's overall depth shall be 30 mm.
requirements.rationale: A cube has equal extent in all three directions.

requirements.statement: The cube's overall height shall be 30 mm.
requirements.rationale: A cube has equal extent in all three directions.

requirements.statement: The cube's side length shall be 30 mm.
requirements.rationale: States the cube's defining dimension explicitly, driving the solid's geometry.

requirements.statement: Each of the three through-holes shall be 10 mm in diameter.
requirements.rationale: The brief specifies 10 mm holes along each axis.

requirements.statement: The part shall have exactly three through-holes, one along each axis, intersecting at the cube's centre.
requirements.rationale: The brief calls for three mutually perpendicular holes through the centre.

assumptions.statement: The part shall be made of PLA (as a 3D-printed material), with no further grade or print-quality specification.
assumptions.rationale: The brief names PLA directly; no other grade or finish is given.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Negligible since PLA is a material family rather than a load-bearing spec; swapping PLA variants has no functional effect given no load case.

assumptions.statement: The three 10 mm holes are mutually orthogonal, each centred on and passing fully through the cube's geometric centre along the X, Y and Z axes respectively.
assumptions.rationale: The brief says 'one along each axis' passing through the centre, implying exact orthogonal intersection, but gives no explicit tolerance on this alignment.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the holes are offset from the true centre or not orthogonal, the resulting internal cavity shape and wall thicknesses at the intersection differ substantially from what is intended.

assumptions.statement: The 10 mm holes are plain through-bores with no specified fit, tolerance class, or fastener/pin interface -- clearance only.
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives no indication the holes mate with a shaft, pin, or fastener.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the holes were meant to be a precision fit for a mating part, the as-printed bore size (subject to FDM shrinkage) may not be usable without rework.

assumptions.statement: No chamfer, fillet, or deburring is required at the sharp internal edges created where the three bores intersect.
assumptions.rationale: The brief does not mention edge treatment at the hole intersections.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Sharp internal edges could be a minor handling/aesthetic issue but are not a structural concern given no load case.

unknowns.question: What is the intended function of the three holes (e.g. alignment/registration feature, pass-through for rods or cables, weight reduction, or purely decorative)?
unknowns.why_it_matters: While it doesn't change the geometry already specified, it could affect whether tighter tolerances, chamfers, or a specific fit are actually needed, which this design currently assumes are not required.
unknowns.suggested_default: Decorative or demonstrative fixture piece with no functional mating requirement

note: Every check passed; held for ASM_HOLE_ALIGNMENT, moderate and irreversible: the brief's own 'three holes through its centre, one along each axis' said back as an assumption.
